---
title: "Body-Weight Dynamics"
description: "Estimation and control of one diet: an energy-balance state-space model, a joint unscented Kalman filter, and a receding-horizon controller."
---

::: {.research-page}

::: {.research-lead}
A scale is a noisy sensor, a diet is an input, and a plateau is a time constant.
:::

The usual arithmetic of dieting, 3,500 kcal per pound, treats the body as a
battery of fixed energy density. It is wrong in three ways that a control
engineer will recognize at once: the mass being lost is a mixture whose
composition changes as you go, a fast water compartment moves pounds on the
scale without moving any tissue, and expenditure adapts to a sustained
deficit with a lag of a few weeks.

Each of those is a state. This project models each one as such, estimates them
together with the subject's personal metabolic parameters from a single noisy reading a
morning, and plans what to eat with a model-predictive controller that
replans every day.

## The presentation

::: {.research-paper}

**Presentation**

[Body-Weight Dynamics →](weight-dynamics.html) walks through the model, the
filter and the controller, with figures generated from a real subject's weigh-ins
and food log. About twenty-five slides, with speaker notes and three backup slides.

:::

## The pieces

- **Model.** Five states (tissue, fat mass, glycogen-bound water, sodium-bound
  water, adaptive thermogenesis) and nine parameters. Tissue follows energy
  balance with an energy density set by Forbes' partition law; the water
  compartments and adaptation are first-order lags on days and weeks.
- **Estimation, in two phases.** Weight-only history identifies the noise by
  maximum likelihood on a local linear trend model. Weight and food together
  identify metabolism, with the parameters appended to the state and estimated
  by an unscented Kalman filter in a coordinate where no sigma point can be
  physically impossible.
- **Control.** A 28-day horizon in weekly blocks, with tissue, not scale weight,
  in both the objective and the safety constraints, so that a fast water drop is
  never mistaken for progress or for danger. Only the first day is eaten.

## Status

The current attempt began on October 26, 2026. With three weigh-ins and two logged days of food, the
filter correctly reports that it has learned almost nothing about the
subject's metabolism yet: every parameter but one still sits on its prior. The deck will
be updated as the record grows.

This is a modeling exercise built on population-level physiology and fitted to
one person's self-reported data. It is not medical advice.

:::
